proofs.proof_tex:
Fix an observed multinomial vector \(\eta\in\Theta_{\mathrm{reg}}(\delta)\), and write \(P_\eta\) for its observed law.  Put
\[
r_x(\eta)=\sum_y\eta_{x1y},\qquad c_x(\eta)=\sum_y\eta_{x0y},\qquad p_x(\eta)=r_x(\eta)+c_x(\eta).
\tag{61}
\]
Because every coordinate of \(\eta\) is at least \(\delta\),
\[
r_x(\eta)\geq K\delta,qquad c_x(\eta)\geq K\delta,qquad p_x(\eta)\geq2K\delta.
\tag{62}
\]
In particular all divisions below are legitimate.  The overlap assumption also gives \(e_x(\eta)=r_x(\eta)/p_x(\eta)\in[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\).

We first put the programs for different observed laws on one fixed feasible cone.  For every response-type cell define
\[
h_{xij}=\frac{a_{xij}}{e_x},\qquad k_{xij}=\frac{b_{xij}}{1-e_x}.
\tag{63}
\]
For a positive cell, \(q_{xij}=a_{xij}/(a_{xij}+b_{xij})\), and hence
\[
\frac{q_{xij}/(1-q_{xij})}{e_x/(1-e_x)}=\frac{h_{xij}}{k_{xij}}.
\tag{64}
\]
With the usual closed-cone interpretation when both masses vanish, the odds restriction is therefore equivalent to membership of the parameter-independent polyhedral cone
\[
\mathcal W_\Gamma=\left\{(h,k):h_{xij},k_{xij}\geq0, Gamma h_{xij}-k_{xij}\geq0, Gamma k_{xij}-h_{xij}\geq0  ext{ for all }x,i,j\right\}.
\tag{65}
\]
The observed-margin and ATE equations become
\[
\begin{split}
r_x(\eta)\sum_i h_{xij}&=\eta_{x1j},\\
c_x(\eta)\sum_j k_{xij}&=\eta_{x0i},\\
\sum_{x,i,j}(j-i)\{r_x(\eta)h_{xij}+c_x(\eta)k_{xij}\}&=t.
\end{split}
\tag{66}
\]
Let \(A_\eta w=b_\eta(t)\) denote (66), where \(w=(h,k)\).  Direct substitution into \(\mathrm{def{:}assignment\mbox{-}cost}\) gives
\[
F_\eta(w)=\sum_{x,i,j}
\frac{r_x(\eta)c_x(\eta)(h_{xij}-k_{xij})^2}
{r_x(\eta)h_{xij}+c_x(\eta)k_{xij}},
\tag{67}
\]
where a summand is zero when \(h_{xij}=k_{xij}=0\).  Indeed, (63) gives \(d_{xij}=e_x(1-e_x)(h_{xij}-k_{xij})\), \(s_{xij}=e_xh_{xij}+(1-e_x)k_{xij}\), and multiplication by \(p_x\) yields (67).  Thus \(\mathrm{thm{:}sharp\mbox{-}frontier}\) and the bijective scaling (63) imply the exact, rather than relaxed, representation
\[
C_{P_\eta}(t)=\min\{F_\eta(w):w\in\mathcal W_\Gamma, A_\eta w=b_\eta(t)\}.
\tag{68}
\]
Every feasible \(w\) in (68) satisfies
\[
\sum_{i,j}h_{xij}=1,qquad \sum_{i,j}k_{xij}=1,qquad 0\leq h_{xij},k_{xij}\leq1,
\tag{69}
\]
by summing the first two groups of equations in (66).  Consequently the minimum in (68) is attained, consistently with \(\mathrm{thm{:}sharp\mbox{-}frontier}\).

We next prove a uniform bound for attained dual multipliers.  If the regular region is empty there is nothing to prove.  In the nonvacuous case the cone in (65) is read in its affine hull after deleting redundant faces.  The strict feasible array supplied by \(\mathrm{ass{:}uniform\mbox{-}primal\mbox{-}margin}\), after (63), lies a computable Euclidean distance \(\gamma_\delta>0\) from every nonredundant face of \(\mathcal W_\Gamma\).  To verify the asserted uniformity rather than assume it, note that the two original odds slacks transform as
\[
\begin{split}
a-\ell_x(a+b)
&=\frac{e_x(1-e_x)}{e_x+\Gamma(1-e_x)}(\Gamma h-k),\\
u_x(a+b)-a
&=\frac{e_x(1-e_x)}{1-e_x+\Gamma e_x}(\Gamma k-h).
\end{split}
\tag{70}
\]
The two displayed factors are bounded above and away from zero on \([\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\); the response-mass inequalities are transformed by the diagonal factors \(e_x\) and \(1-e_x\).  Hence the declared slack \(\delta\) gives a positive lower bound on every normalized inequality slack in (65).  Dividing that lower bound by the largest norm of the finitely many face normals gives such a \(\gamma_\delta\).  This construction uses only \(\delta,\varepsilon,\Gamma,K\), and \(|\mathcal X|\), so \(\gamma_\delta\) is computable.

The equality operator in (66) has full row rank, uniformly over the cell simplex satisfying (62).  The margin rows have disjoint supports and norms at least \(K\delta\sqrt K\).  Moreover, for any fixed \(x\), take a vector in the kernel of all margin rows whose only nonzero entries are \(h_{x,0,0}=1\) and \(h_{x,1,0}=-1\).  Its inner product with the ATE row is \(r_x(\eta)\), which is at least \(K\delta\) by (62).  Thus the ATE row is not in the span of the margin rows.  Continuity of singular values on the compact set
\[
\Delta_\delta=\left\{\eta:\eta_{xzy}\geq\delta, sum_{x,z,y}\eta_{xzy}=1\right\}
\tag{71}
\]
therefore gives the computable positive number
\[
\sigma_\delta=\min_{\eta\in\Delta_\delta}\sigma_{\min}(A_\eta)>0.
\tag{72}
\]
Equivalently, the right inverse
\[
R_\eta=A_\eta^{\mathsf T}(A_\eta A_\eta^{\mathsf T})^{-1}
\tag{73}
\]
satisfies \(\|R_\eta\|_{2\to2}\leq\sigma_\delta^{-1}\).  The exceptional equality-odds case \(\Gamma=1\) has \(q_{xij}=e_x\), so consistency identifies the ATE as \(\sum_xp_x\{E_P(Y\mid Z=1,X=x)-E_P(Y\mid Z=0,X=x)\}\) and \(D_P\) is a singleton.  Hence it cannot produce a nonempty \(\mathcal T_0\subset\operatorname{int}D_P\); the asserted regular-profile conclusion is then vacuous.  Thus (72) covers every nonvacuous case.

For \(y=(\alpha,\beta,\lambda)\), use the sign convention
\[
\mathcal L_\eta(w;y)=F_\eta(w)+y^{\mathsf T}\{b_\eta(t)-A_\eta w\}.
\tag{74}
\]
Under (63), cellwise minimization of (74) over \(\mathcal W_\Gamma\) is exactly the constraint in \(\mathrm{def{:}dual}\): writing \(r_xh_{xij}+c_xk_{xij}=p_xs_{xij}\) and \(r_xh_{xij}=p_xs_{xij}q_{xij}\), its coefficient along a cell ray is
\[
p_xs_{xij}\left\{
\frac{(q_{xij}-e_x)^2}{e_x(1-e_x)}
-q_{xij}\alpha_{xj}-(1-q_{xij})\beta_{xi}-\lambda(j-i)
\right\}.
\tag{75}
\]
Therefore \(\mathrm{thm{:}explicit\mbox{-}dual}\) supplies an attained \(y_\eta(t)\) satisfying the saddle identity
\[
C_{P_\eta}(t)=\inf_{w\in\mathcal W_\Gamma}\mathcal L_\eta(w;y_\eta(t)).
\tag{76}
\]

Let \(w^\circ\) be the strict feasible point above, set \(\tau_\delta=\gamma_\delta\sigma_\delta/2\), and let \(z\) be any unit vector in the equality space.  From (73),
\[
w^\pm=w^\circ\pm\tau_\delta R_\eta z\in\mathcal W_\Gamma,qquad
A_\eta w^\pm=b_\eta(t)\pm\tau_\delta z.
\tag{77}
\]
The points in (77) range over a compact set: (69) bounds \(w^\circ\), and the correction has Euclidean norm at most \(\gamma_\delta/2\).  Formula (67), (62), and
\[
0\leq
\frac{r c(h-k)^2}{rh+ck}
\leq\frac{(h+k)^2}{K\delta(h+k)}
=\frac{h+k}{K\delta}
\tag{78}
\]
show that \(F_\eta(w^\pm)\leq\overline F_\delta<\infty\) for a computable \(\overline F_\delta\).  Evaluate (76) at the two points in (77).  Since \(C_{P_\eta}(t)\geq0\),
\[
\begin{split}
\tau_\delta y_\eta(t)^{\mathsf T}z
&\leq F_\eta(w^+)-C_{P_\eta}(t)\leq\overline F_\delta,\\
-\tau_\delta y_\eta(t)^{\mathsf T}z
&\leq F_\eta(w^-)-C_{P_\eta}(t)\leq\overline F_\delta.
\end{split}
\tag{79}
\]
Taking the supremum over unit \(z\), and converting Euclidean to \(\ell_1\) norm in the \(d=2|\mathcal X|K+1\) dimensional equality space, gives
\[
\|y_\eta(t)\|_1\leq
B_\delta:=\frac{\sqrt d\,\overline F_\delta}{\tau_\delta}<\infty
\quad\text{uniformly in }\eta\in\Theta_{\mathrm{reg}}(\delta), t\in\mathcal T_0.
\tag{80}
\]
Equations (70)--(73), (78), and (80) are an explicit finite-dimensional recipe for \(B_\delta\); in particular, no active-set stability is being presumed.

We now compare two laws correctly.  Let \(\eta,\eta'\in\Theta_{\mathrm{reg}}(\delta)\), fix the same \(t\in\mathcal T_0\), put \(d_\infty=\|\eta-\eta'\|_\infty\), and let \(w'\) be a primal optimizer for \((\eta',t)\).  For
\[
\psi_{r,c}(h,k)=\frac{rc(h-k)^2}{rh+ck},
\]
the denominator bound in (62) and \(|h-k|\leq h+k\) give, with \(m=K\delta\),
\[
|\partial_r\psi_{r,c}(h,k)|\leq\frac{h+k}{m}+\frac{h}{m^2},qquad
|\partial_c\psi_{r,c}(h,k)|\leq\frac{h+k}{m}+\frac{k}{m^2}.
\tag{81}
\]
The assertion is also valid at \(h=k=0\), where the function is identically zero in \((r,c)\).  Since \(|r_x(\eta)-r_x(\eta')|\) and \(|c_x(\eta)-c_x(\eta')|\) are at most \(K d_\infty\), summing (81) and using (69) yields
\[
|F_\eta(w')-F_{\eta'}(w')|
\leq K_F d_\infty,qquad
K_F=2|\mathcal X|K\left(\frac{2}{m}+\frac{1}{m^2}\right).
\tag{82}
\]
Likewise, direct use of (66) and (69) gives
\[
\left\|\{b_\eta(t)-A_\eta w'\}-\{b_{\eta'}(t)-A_{\eta'}w'\}\right\|_\infty
\leq K_A d_\infty,
\tag{83}
\]
where one may take
\[
K_A=\max\{1+K, 2|\mathcal X|K(K-1)\}.
\tag{84}
\]
Indeed, a margin row in (83) is bounded by \(d_\infty+Kd_\infty\), while the ATE row is bounded by \((K-1)\sum_x\{|r_x-r_x'|+|c_x-c_x'|\}\).

Here is the sensitivity step that remains valid when coefficients and odds faces move.  Use the attained dual \(y_\eta(t)\) only in its own saddle identity (76), and evaluate that identity at the other problem's primal optimizer \(w'\).  Since \(w'\in\mathcal W_\Gamma\) and \(b_{\eta'}(t)-A_{\eta'}w'=0\), equations (76), (80), (82), and (83) imply
\[
\begin{split}
C_{P_\eta}(t)
&\leq \mathcal L_\eta(w';y_\eta(t))\\
&=C_{P_{\eta'}}(t)+F_\eta(w')-F_{\eta'}(w')
+y_\eta(t)^{\mathsf T}\{b_\eta(t)-A_\eta w'\}\\
&\leq C_{P_{\eta'}}(t)+(K_F+B_\delta K_A)d_\infty.
\end{split}
\tag{85}
\]
Interchanging \(\eta\) and \(\eta'\) proves
\[
|C_{P_\eta}(t)-C_{P_{\eta'}}(t)|
\leq(K_F+B_\delta K_A)\|\eta-\eta'\|_\infty.
\tag{86}
\]
No dual vector in (85) is asserted to be feasible for the other law.  This is a cross-parameter saddle comparison on the common cone (65), not transport of a dual certificate.  By \(\mathrm{def{:}regular\mbox{-}profile\mbox{-}band}\),
\[
L_{\mathrm{reg}}(\delta)\leq K_F+B_\delta K_A<\infty.
\tag{87}
\]
For example,
\[
\mathfrak B_\delta=(1+K_F+K_A)(1+B_\delta)
\tag{88}
\]
is simultaneously a computable uniform \(\ell_1\)-bound on the attained cellwise dual multipliers and an upper bound for the modulus in (87).  This proves the theorem's deterministic and computability assertions.

It remains to prove the simultaneous finite-sample statement.  For a fixed multinomial coordinate, let \(U\) be its cell indicator and let \(p=E_PU\).  If
\[
g(\lambda)=\log E_P\exp\{\lambda(U-p)\},
\]
then \(g(0)=g'(0)=0\), while \(g''(\lambda)\) is the variance of a Bernoulli variable under exponential tilting and is at most \(1/4\).  Two integrations give
\[
E_P\exp\{\lambda(U-p)\}\leq\exp(\lambda^2/8).
\tag{89}
\]
Independence in \(\mathrm{ass{:}iid\mbox{-}sampling}\), Markov's inequality, and minimization at \(\lambda=4r_n\) therefore yield
\[
P\{|\widehat\theta_k-\theta_k|>r_n\}
\leq2\exp(-2nr_n^2)=\frac{\alpha}{M}.
\tag{90}
\]
A union bound over the \(M\) cells proves
\[
P\{\|\widehat\theta-\theta\|_\infty\leq r_n\}\geq1-\alpha.
\tag{91}
\]
On the event in (91), the assumed membership \(\theta\in\Theta_{\mathrm{reg}}(\delta)\) implies \(\theta\in\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\).  Hence, directly from the definitions of the two envelopes, simultaneously for every \(t\in\mathcal T_0\),
\[
\underline C_n(t)\leq C_P(t)\leq\overline C_n(t).
\tag{92}
\]
Any two multinomial vectors in \(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\) are at \(\ell_\infty\)-distance at most \(2r_n\).  Applying the definition of \(L_{\mathrm{reg}}(\delta)\), then taking the supremum and infimum over that same set, gives on the event in (91), again simultaneously in \(t\),
\[
0\leq\overline C_n(t)-\underline C_n(t)
\leq2L_{\mathrm{reg}}(\delta)r_n.
\tag{93}
\]
Together, (87), (91), (92), and (93) prove every assertion.

prose_updates.tldr: A finite observed law is lifted to one joint law of treatment and both potential outcomes, and the least Pearson assignment information needed to support each ATE is profiled. The attained sharp frontier has a perspective SOCP and explicit dual. For binary outcomes, a treatment-independent garbling removes the minority discordant response type without imposing monotone treatment response and without increasing any convex assignment cost; this yields the complete six-face scalar catalog and a squared-correlation null identity. An explicit embedding into the published Ishikawa--He--Kanamori Neyman-divergence Jensen--CMC program proves the same-budget separation \(9/70>9/91\). On a named uniformly Slater-regular multinomial region, a fixed-odds-cone parametrization, a uniform equality right inverse, and bounded attained cellwise dual multipliers yield a finite-sample \(O(n^{-1/2})\) profile diameter without transporting a dual certificate between laws; a contiguous boundary pair shows that honest bands must retain infinite diameter at a finite-to-infinite null-cost boundary.

project_justification.fill: The project profiles the exact full-law Pearson cost, certifies it by primal and dual conic programs, solves the binary geometry, embeds the full-law model into the published Jensen--CMC program with identical budget normalization, and pairs a finite-sample regular-region diameter theorem based on a common fixed odds cone and uniformly bounded attained multipliers with a contiguous boundary lower bound.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: All nuisance quantities are multinomial cell probabilities. Simultaneous cell-frequency concentration is combined with a fixed-odds-cone parametric saddle comparison: uniform primal slack bounds the attained dual multipliers, and each multiplier is used only for its own observed law. This gives the finite-sample regular-region band; the open local theory concerns an estimated directional derivative under weaker facial regularity.

prose_updates.related_work: Zhang and Zhao motivate average rather than worst-case assignment distortion and prove sharp bounds for each average potential outcome, but their discussion explicitly withholds joint ATE attainment. Ishikawa, He, and Kanamori define an observed-policy-first \(f\)-divergence in their equation (10), apply Jensen in equation (12), and combine the relaxed divergence with CMC in equation (14). The full-law comparison theorem uses their Neyman generator and proves the strict same-budget ATE-slice separation \(9/70>9/91\). Balke and Pearl supply the finite response-type representation, and Manski supplies the substantive monotone-response benchmark; the binary garbling result instead derives monotone support for an extremal compatible law without assuming monotone treatment response of the population. The regular finite-sample theorem rescales response-type masses onto a common odds cone, derives a uniform right-inverse and multiplier bound from the declared Slater margin, and compares different observed laws through the saddle identity at each law rather than reusing a moved dual certificate. Duan, Zhang, and Zhang derive directional derivatives for finite-valued Slater-regular SOCP values, while Fang and Santos and Firpo, Galvao, and Parker supply derivative-aware statistical inference; extending those tools through zero perspective cells and moving faces remains the open tangent-inference question.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The interior binary stationarity equation is generically quintic, so the exact catalog isolates a unique algebraic root and does not promise universal radical formulas. The regular-profile constant depends on both the fixed-cone interior radius and the smallest singular value of the equality operator, and can deteriorate as the observed-cell or Slater margin \(\delta\) approaches zero. The boundary lower bound shows that this deterioration reflects a genuine statistical discontinuity at the null-feasibility boundary.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The sharpness, dual attainment, garbling, scalar catalog, explicit published-program embedding, strict relaxation gap, regular-region finite-sample diameter, and boundary impossibility are theorem claims proved in the note. The regular diameter proof controls coefficient movement through a common fixed odds cone and a law-specific saddle comparison; it does not claim stability of an active set or feasibility of one law's dual certificate at another law. Uniform tangent inference under weaker facial regularity and adaptive derivative-bootstrap inversion remain open. The \(\Gamma=1\) specialization is retained only as a regression corollary. The application target is a prespecified categorical mercury score and finite covariate stratification; it does not claim to recover the original continuous-outcome NHANES estimand.

statement_notes.justification: This theorem converts multinomial concentration into an honest finite-sample simultaneous band with \(O(n^{-1/2})\) diameter on a named interior region, using a common-cone saddle comparison that remains valid when observed-law coefficients move.
statement_notes.gap: ZhangZhao2026AverageCase gives regular bands for armwise sensitivity curves; it does not control the finite-sample diameter of a jointly compatible ATE cost frontier through a uniform fixed-cone Slater and multiplier modulus.
statement_notes.consumer: The categorical-mercury analysis obtains a finite-width simultaneous frontier band whenever its prespecified cells and ATE range satisfy the reported observed-cell, cone-slack, and equality-rank margins.
